checks.label: H₂ flow vs stack demand
checks.what: Measured H₂ flow compared with the flow the stack current requires at 80 % utilisation.
checks.hint: Negative: supply restriction (regulator, valve, upstream pressure, filter). Positive: leak or flow-meter error.

checks.label: Fuel utilisation
checks.what: Share of the H₂ that the Faraday current oxidises. Above 0.88 the anode risks fuel starvation and nickel re-oxidation.
checks.hint: High utilisation with a normal current means too little H₂ is arriving. Check supply pressure and the H₂ regulator.

checks.label: Air flow vs heat-balance need
checks.what: Shortfall of the measured air flow against the flow that removes the stack heat at a 97 K temperature rise.
checks.hint: Deficit: blower fade, blocked air filter, closed damper or high air-path ΔP. The stack then runs hotter.

checks.label: Blower power vs flow
checks.what: Blower power compared with what the blower law predicts for the measured air flow and ambient temperature.
checks.hint: Excess power for the flow delivered: worn blower, fouled impeller, motor or VFD problem, or extra resistance in the air path.

checks.label: Air ratio (O₂ fed / O₂ consumed)
checks.what: How much more oxygen is supplied than the cells consume. Cooling, not oxygen demand, sets it (design about 11).
checks.hint: Low: air starvation risk and hot stack. High: wasted blower power and over-cooling.

checks.label: Cathode temperature rise
checks.what: Outlet minus inlet air temperature (15-min mean). The ceramic cells tolerate at most 100 K across the stack; the warning starts at 103 K so that the short overshoots seen during load changes on this plant do not raise alerts.
checks.hint: Above the band: more air, lower load, or find the cause (blower, maldistribution). Do not keep running above 108 K.

checks.label: Stack heat balance
checks.what: Heat carried away by the measured air flow and temperature rise, compared with the heat the cell reaction releases.
checks.hint: A mismatch means a reading is wrong or heat goes somewhere unexpected: thermocouple drift, air maldistribution, a leak or an internal fault.

checks.label: Cathode inlet vs setpoint
checks.what: Cathode inlet temperature minus its 650 °C setpoint.
checks.hint: Check the air preheater, the flue gas path and the temperature controller.

checks.label: Afterburner temperature
checks.what: Tail-gas combustor outlet. Too low: incomplete burn-out. Too high: damage to the catalyst and exchangers.
checks.hint: Low: unburned H₂ may slip or the burner is not lit. High: excess fuel reaching the burner.

checks.label: DC power vs current × voltage
checks.what: Difference between the DC power reading and stack current times voltage times the cells in series.
checks.hint: A mismatch means a bad sensor or a wiring or scaling error on the DC side.

checks.label: Net power balance
checks.what: Net AC power minus (DC power × inverter efficiency − blowers − auxiliaries).
checks.hint: A mismatch means the inverter is losing more than expected, or a parasitic load is not being counted.

checks.label: Stack voltage vs new-stack model
checks.what: Cell voltage below what a new stack gives at the same current, temperature and utilisation. 10 % is end of life.
checks.hint: A steady rise is ageing: plan maintenance. A sudden step points to a fault such as a hot spot, leak or fuel starvation.

checks.label: Steam vs heat balance
checks.what: Steam output compared with the heat the plant should be leaving in the exhaust.
checks.hint: Low: HRSG fouling, feedwater shortage, bypassed exhaust. High: flow-meter error.

checks.label: Flue gas leaving HRSG
checks.what: Exhaust temperature to the stack (design about 133 °C).
checks.hint: High: HRSG fouling or low feedwater flow, heat is being wasted. Low: over-extraction, risk of condensation.

checks.label: Anode-cathode ΔP
checks.what: Pressure difference across the thin ceramic electrolyte. Above 30 mbar the cells or seals can break.
checks.hint: Spikes point to a valve or regulator hunting or a blocked line. Check both manifold pressure controls.

checks.label: Anode recycle vs expected
checks.what: Measured anode recycle flow compared with the flow the anode-loop mass balance requires.
checks.hint: Low recycle means less steam at the anode inlet and a risk of nickel oxidation. Check the recycle blower or ejector and its valves.
